description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:406-413 — verify_embedded_scts takes &Certificate parameters, then immediately re-encodes them to DER (encode_to_vec) so it can call verify_sct_for_precert(&[u8], &[u8]).

The caller almost certainly has the original DER bytes available (they parsed the Certificate FROM those bytes). The re-encode is wasted work, AND introduces the round-trip canonicalization risk discussed in PKIX-q74z.5 (re-encoded TBS may differ from the original DER if the cert was non-canonically encoded).

For the round-trip canonicalization issue specifically: if the caller parsed leaf from PEM and re-encodes, the re-encoded TBS might not match what the log signed over (the log signed over the original-parse-via-cryptography bytes, which might use different INTEGER encoding than x509-cert produces). Today verify_embedded_scts produces wrong signed-input bytes in that case, returning Ok(0) instead of correct counts.

Suggested fix: take &[u8] (DER bytes) as input alongside the &Certificate, OR change the signature to take only DER and parse internally. Match what tbs_without_sct_list does (parse from DER directly). This also fixes the canonicalization issue.

Lower-priority because the re-encode bug is masked by the bigger round-trip dependency (PKIX-q74z.5) and most real CT-logged certs survive both round-trips. But the API shape locks in an unnecessary double-conversion.
title: verify_embedded_scts: leaf+issuer DER re-encoded in N=1 case wastes work since cert was already provided as Certificate
